_about: Appendix D of the suite results document, the one-page glossary (round 2, after OWNER-REVIEW-SAMPLE-1.md): `entries` is a list of {term, definition, see} (see: other terms, optional); the generator prints them in alphabetical order in two columns. Twenty-five terms (the owner's review: about 25, one page; timing class and re-evaluation are in I.2, I.4 and the README's long form), the ones a reader needs to interpret the evidence: scenario against execution, finding, inconclusive, not exercised (not implemented via MCP), by design, agreement depth, wall, server and backend time, the host-cache heuristic, column and header label, the stated stop, and the few the tables need. The long form (every term of the suite) is the glossary section of the suite's README (`readme`: path and section; `commit` pins it by hand, else the generator reads the commit that last touched the README in the checkout); `lead` is printed above the entries with that pin. `records_key.lead` heads the record key the generator prints before the entries from the manifest's ground_truth.records (re-verification N-1: the key before the glossary, linked from every matrix's legend and from the compact key of I.3). Definitions follow the suite's README, checks.py, compare.py, report.py and gate.py as of c11db9dd, and SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 4. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*; placeholders as in overview.json.

_assumes._note: The literal numbers this file's prose may carry, each with its source: constants of the SPEC, of the manifest v4 (lengths, budgets, expected runs), of the service's table or of the harness, never a figure of a run (those are placeholders the generator fills). tests/test_doc.py fails on a number the prose carries that is listed neither here nor as a placeholder; add a constant here with its source, never a run's figure.
_assumes.1: L - k + 1 (SPEC section 4.1); max(1 s, the budget) (checks.py)
_assumes.2: the sampler's 2 s interval (sampler.py); DUST below 2 (areas.py)
_assumes.250: the finalisation reserve in ms (SPEC section 4.5)

readme.pin: the checks commit and the manifest version named on the title page and in I.4; the README section states the commit it was written for

lead: The terms a reader needs to interpret the evidence, in one page; the long form of every term of the suite is the glossary section of `{readme_path}` as of commit {readme_commit}, pinned to the checks and the manifest version this document names, so that an archived report stays interpretable. The record key precedes the entries; the matrices' legends link to it.

entries.definition: One frozen test of the manifest: an id (family prefix and number, e.g. R-pos-0013), a route, the exact request, the ground truth, the expectations (check and arguments), the MCP mapping, a timing class, a repeat count, tags. The tables' test id is the scenario id.

One request of one scenario on one arm: status, wall and server times, host-cache state, checks, outcome. Repeat 0 is the arm's first; an MCP scenario the service can express has two (cold, then warm), every tenth scenario and chapter D have direct repeats. Execution counts and scenario counts are stated apart.

A chapter is an area (R resolve, T traverse, P and L patterns, X peptides, M mismatches, Q predicates, C capabilities, N negatives, D determinism); a family the scenarios sharing an id prefix; a unit one builder template, one property, varied over one dimension, printed as one table. Appendix E maps every id to its unit's page.

A route to the host: direct-local (mex to the container's port), direct-remote (a laptop through the public URL and the nginx front), mcp (the search service's tools, calling the host over the public URL). direct-local is the reference arm of the MCP comparison.

From the checks by precedence: fail, finding, inconclusive, pass; error (no HTTP answer, an undecodable body, a check that raised) counts with the failures; not implemented via MCP and service-side by design are decided without the checks. Over repeats: the common outcome, else the worst (mixed, mark m).

A stated bound or SPEC promise the host broke without failing the request: a 200 past its budget, an allowed 503 deadline more than max(1 s, the budget) late, a walk stopped before its budget or run past it beyond its pieces. Counted apart from failures (verdict FINDINGS); the detail block quotes the rule and the overrun.

The test could not test its property on this answer: an allowed 503 deadline, a list a legitimate statement hides the source in, a walk a stated limit stopped first, a stop that was the property and did not happen, nothing to compare, no property field exposed, a host state. Never a pass, never a failure; on a gated arm, in the policy's selection and not declared exempt, it blocks the gate (I.1 counts those).

The request cannot be asked through the MCP tools: the manifest marks it, or a by-design case names the missing argument (support, `bounds.max_query_bp`, graph, a protocol body). The cell says not exercised, never ok; the service's own refusal, when recorded, is under the row or in appendix B. A known limit, not coverage.

The MCP arm legitimately differs because the service refused before host execution, relayed the host's refusal under its own code, answered after normalising the request, or set a value the request did not name, as its table documents. Verified when the direct answer matched the case's host side and the MCP answer its service side; else mark u.

An MCP execution the service ended by its own limit before the host answered (`resolve_timeout` at its deadline for the host call, a relayed `traversal_resolve_deadline` or /pattern deadline): adjudicated inconclusive when the service's own timing shows the limit was reachable, a failure otherwise. The raw check lines are kept as the intermediate evaluation.

The direct arms per scenario: identical (same digest), same checks, timing (a time limitation alone), not comparable, disagree. mcp against the reference arm, check by check: agree, not comparable, disagree; not implemented and by design apart. Depth of an agreement: fully checked (every expected property check on both arms), partial, generic checks only, a refusal. A disagreement fails the run.

Two scenarios' answers compared on one arm: `same_answer`, `prefix_equals` (resolves of pieces of one sequence agree on their common k-mers), subset, `zero_equals_absent`; pass, fail, inconclusive (no two profiles to compare) or not exposed. A failed relation fails the run (appendix C).

A column label is a taxid, one column of the annotation, with one or many records: it supports an in-graph k-mer whose row carries it. A header label is an accession.version, one record of a column reached through the coordinates: it supports a k-mer when a coordinate of its column at that row maps to the record; with support trace only while consecutive k-mers have consecutive coordinates (SPEC 4.2).

A k-mer is k = {k} bases, a node of this basic graph (forward strand only: a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes); a query of L bases has L - k + 1, numbered from 0. Runs are 0-based half-open intervals of k-mer starts: `graph_runs` the in-graph k-mers, a label's runs those it supports, `kmers_supported` their count.

`bounds.time_budget_ms` of a /resolve (opt-in: without it no deadline), `time_budget_ms` of a /pattern, the strategy's budget of a /traverse: lowered to the server's cap and stated in limits.clamped when lowered. A /resolve keeps 250 ms to build the answer: the work stops at the budget less the reserve; a budget not above it is refused (SPEC 4.5).

A /resolve 200 that stopped at its budget less the reserve and says so in its stop block (reason time, `resolved_kmers`, `query_kmers`, `resolved_bp`, `remainder_from_bp`): exactly the resolve of the first `resolved_kmers` k-mers, the prefix; the rest is resolved from `remainder_from_bp`. A stop that cannot have happened fails the checks that met it. Not observed in this run.

The 503 with code deadline /resolve and /pattern answer when the answer cannot be built and written within the budget: nothing partial. Allowed under load where the request names a budget, so inconclusive; a finding when more than max(1 s, the budget) late (the unpolled pieces of SPEC 4.5); a failure on a /resolve without a budget.

Wall: a direct execution from sending the request to the last byte on an established connection (connect time apart); an MCP execution the whole tool interaction. Server: the host's `timing.elapsed_ms`, in brackets; none on a refusal or 503. Backend: the host call as the service measured it, after be; its other phases are submit, queue, terminal lag, paging.

A recency heuristic over all arms, recorded per execution, not a measured cache: cold, the scenario's first execution to reach the host; warm, started within {warm_window_s} s of another ending on the host; aged, later (unknown); not reached, never seen by the host. An MCP pair is cold then warm; a direct time is warm unless marked c, a or i (warm after an interrupted execution, left out of aggregates).

The nginx reverse proxy behind the public URL; every arm but direct-local goes through it. Front cost: direct-remote minus direct-local on host-warm pairs, net of the server time. Connect time: the set-up of a fresh connection (TCP, TLS), recorded apart from the wall.

docker stats of the staging and `sra_all` (Logan indexing) containers and the host load average, sampled every 2 s on mex and joined to each execution: the shared host's context, not the request's cost. The caveat is stated when the `sra_all` CPU mean exceeds {load_caveat_sra_cpu_pct} % or the load1 mean {load_caveat_load1}: such timings are not the baseline.

The run's word, in this order: INCOMPLETE (an arm unfinished, a planned execution unrecorded), FAIL (a failed or errored execution, a disagreement, a failed relation), FINDINGS, INCONCLUSIVE (nothing passed, a group tested nothing, two deployments), PASS; EMPTY and UNVERIFIED (a status-only stub). Inconclusive executions are counted after it, never as passes.

The strict judgement against a policy that pins the manifest, relations, index and by-design table and names the gated arms (mcp, direct-local): it fails on anything missing, any non-pass on a gated arm, any mark it cannot explain, any disagreement, any required relation not passed, configuration evidence not recorded live. The declared file is the owner's reasoned exemptions, the only other way past; printed in full.

A test is clean when every arm is a pass, not exercised via MCP, a verified by-design pair, or had no planned execution: one cell or line, no claim beyond those states. Any other test carries a footnote digit on its offending cells and a detail block after its table (numbering restarts per chapter).

One indexed sequence of the ground truth, named by its accession.version (header label), in a taxid column (column label): the {n_records} genomes of the search service's validation set, fetched at the indexed version. A window is a stretch of a record's forward strand cut at a seeded position (ACGT only, DUST below 2, unique on either strand). The tables use the keys below.

records_key.lead: The record abbreviations of the matrices (the manifest's ground truth; the accession.version is the record's header label, the taxid its column label):
records_key.source: the manifest's ground_truth.records (key, label, accession, taxid, kingdom, length, records in column, code, last in column), printed by the generator in full
